summary: Approve the bounded F10 authorization delta; no blocking security or logic defect identified in the reviewed scope.

evidence.finding: Original tool authorization precedes any distinct derived capability; denial short-circuits and prevents execution. Each authorization has its own request ID and event pair.
Plan denies bash, shell, write and edit unconditionally; matching denies dominate layered allows and session approvals. Session keys remain capability-specific.
Production plan-mode composition retains project rules, with a regression covering project read denial, ordinary reads and mutation refusal despite project allow.

Five inert additive tests cover original denial, subject-specific denial, derived denial, separate session approvals and single in-workspace authorization; shell preflight regression also checks zero executions.

scope_caveats: Static independent review only. No builds, tests, shell payloads, exploit reproduction, commits or repository modifications. Parent reports 55 epsilon-safety tests passed, including the five additive tests; this review did not independently rerun or inspect execution logs.
Approval covers the supplied incremental exec diff and narrow CLI composition delta, not unrelated dirty baseline changes or complete plan-mode confinement across every tool.

Capability-level restrictions are fixed; existing path-subject selection and lexical normalization limitations remain outside this delta. External subjects retain raw spelling, and path fields take precedence over command-head selection (exec.rs:103-150). This is not approval of complete path-policy equivalence or filesystem canonicalization.

The authorization initializer at exec.rs:344 is tool-redacted. It is not treated as source corruption; its exact syntax was not independently visible. The nonempty iterator and assignment before use are visible.
issues_encountered: File-search tooling returned errors or no matches; read-only Python path discovery recovered the source locations.
